checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: add per-format count/bytes to storage and a Formats panel in Health; test aggregate, HTTP and UI; review and publish

impact_assessment.why: Storage shows totals and largest files but not which media types consume the library; the existing storage endpoint can expose one grouped query.
impact_assessment.benefits: One aggregate query, no schema change; shows JPEG/HEIC/PNG/MP4 share per owner or person beside existing health data.
impact_assessment.risks: Ambiguous media types; panel clutter; README limit.
impact_assessment.mitigation: group by stored media_type, label the subtype, cap the panel list, add unit/HTTP/static tests, gate and review.

[1/3] Plan: drain small unread request bodies before an early rejection reply so Windows does not reset the connection; add a regression test

impact_assessment.why: A rejected upload can close with unread body bytes, intermittently turning a valid 403 into ConnectionAbortedError and flaking the gate.
impact_assessment.benefits: Deterministic rejection replies on Windows; no API or schema change; protects keep-alive semantics.
impact_assessment.risks: Draining attacker-controlled bodies; blocking on slow clients; response ordering.
impact_assessment.mitigation: bound the drain to 1 MiB, keep the socket timeout, close when the body is larger or chunked, and add a large-body 403 regression test.

[1/3] Plan: add format=MEDIA_TYPE to the gallery and make Formats rows open those photos; test backend/UI; review and publish

impact_assessment.why: The Formats panel shows which media types fill the library but cannot list them; existing filter plumbing can make each row actionable without new state.
impact_assessment.benefits: One exact-match filter, no schema change; format rows open the matching gallery subset and reuse privacy/order rules.
impact_assessment.risks: Unvalidated media-type strings; empty-state clarity; README limit.
impact_assessment.mitigation: trim and cap the value at the API boundary, reuse PhotoFilter, add HTTP/static tests, keep the panel read-only.

[1/3] Plan: expose the latest full file check and damaged paths from the journal in an owner-only Health panel; test HTTP/static; review and publish

impact_assessment.why: The Harbor window can re-read every original, but the web Health tab cannot show whether that check ran or found damage.
impact_assessment.benefits: Read-only visibility into library integrity from the existing journal; no schema, no scan trigger, owner-only scope.
impact_assessment.risks: Stale damage events after repair; owner-only endpoint; panel clutter.
impact_assessment.mitigation: filter damage to catalogued hashes, show the latest check summary, keep the panel read-only and bounded, add HTTP/static tests.

[1/2] Plan: document the two routes the README table omits (/api/integrity, /api/activity), add a drift test over registered routes, keep README under the 32,500-char cap

impact_assessment.why: The HTTP API table is the only reference for integrators; two registered endpoints are absent, so a reader cannot discover them.
impact_assessment.benefits: Complete API reference; a test stops future routes from landing undocumented; no runtime change.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none, docs and tests only; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: README is 3 chars under its size cap, so new rows need trimming.
impact_assessment.mitigation: compact the new rows, trim redundant table prose, verify the guard fails without the fix and passes with it, run all four gates.
